patch.value: Agent-environment programme: pm as the task substrate, verifier, and trajectory source for RL training, evaluation, benchmarking and simulation workflows

Programme-level container, filed 2026-07-31 because the capability already exists in pieces and has no single owner. Duplicate check: searched RL, environment, episode, trajectory, benchmark, corpus generator and deterministic reset lineages; every constituent item was found and none is duplicated here. This epic organizes them and names what is missing between them; it does not restate their scope and does not re-parent them, since each is correctly parented by the capability it modifies.

Why a programme rather than another capability epic. The existing eighteen epics partition the product by subsystem - storage, graph, MCP, scale, schema. This work cuts across four of them at once and is coherent only when read end to end. Today its constituent items are parented in four different places: pm-nfrhf0 (the environment-author story) and pm-li2fj5 (episode substrate) under pm-8jdc schema and config; pm-qd6gvf (trajectory projection) under pm-o2kc storage and history; pm-8bgeye (attested context reads) and pm-tch9cs (fleet-amortized assembly) under pm-9rxu scale-out. Nothing reads them as one deliverable, so no one owns the seams between them. This follows the pattern already established by pm-wjfa, pm-92if and pm-n7rr, which are cross-cutting programmes rather than subsystems.

What already exists and is shipped, so the programme starts from a real base rather than a blank one. pm-rbcvt2 delivered reproducible workspace instances with seeded identifiers, an injectable clock and byte-identical construction, which is the reset primitive any environment needs. pm-mi2x delivered the scale benchmark harness with synthetic 10k, 100k and 1M item generators plus latency, memory and token baselines. pm-vv2lti corrected those fixtures so population shape varies rather than only size. The immutable history stream, hash-chained and restorable to any version, is the trajectory source. Together these are most of a usable environment substrate; what is missing is the contract that presents them as one.

The four seams this epic owns, none of which belongs to a single constituent item.

First, episode identity across surfaces and processes. An episode spans several pm invocations, some through the CLI and some through MCP, and the only per-session key today is agent_instance. pm-1zhfls proves that key is already unreliable for provenance because one session records different dimensions depending on surface, and pm-rbg1qo shows no role or topic has ever been recorded. Without a stable, labelled episode key, trajectory projection cannot group and fleet analytics cannot aggregate. This is the programme's binding prerequisite rather than a nice-to-have.

Second, the verdict contract. pm-li2fj5 composes a computed verdict into the episode unit. What is undefined is the boundary between a verdict pm computes from recorded state - which is auditable, reproducible and the whole point - and a reward an environment author computes outside pm. Getting that boundary wrong in either direction is costly: too narrow and every author reimplements state inspection, too wide and pm acquires opinions about reward shaping that belong to the training loop.

Third, the observation contract. pm-8bgeye makes an assembly attestable and pm-tch9cs shares assemblies across a fleet. An environment needs a bounded observation whose token cost is declared before the call, so a training run can budget. That is the same requirement as pm-5t33or's contract-declared output budgets, viewed from the environment side, and the two should resolve to one mechanism rather than two.

Fourth, non-PM domains. pm-t4d7nz requires non-PM systems to be buildable on SDK primitives alone. An RL environment is the most demanding such system, because it needs reset, step, observe and score with reproducibility guarantees, and it therefore functions as the acceptance test for that milestone. pm-z5pmf8 blocks it directly: while the SDK's lifecycle surface re-exports CLI command modules, an environment author cannot compose a step from primitives without depending on the CLI layer.

Deliberately out of scope: any opinion about model training, reward shaping, or a specific RL framework. pm supplies substrate - reproducible state, bounded observation, recorded trajectory, computed verdict - and stops there.

An environment author can run a complete episode - reset, step, observe, score - through public SDK primitives alone, with no import from src/cli and no shelling out, demonstrated by a worked example under docs/examples; A stable episode identity spans every surface and process an episode touches, is recorded in the immutable stream, and groups a trajectory correctly when a session mixes CLI and MCP calls; The boundary between a pm-computed verdict and an author-computed reward is stated as a contract, with pm's side reproducible from recorded state and independently checkable; Observation cost is declared before the call and honoured, so a training loop can budget tokens per step without measuring empirically; The programme's own scale claim is proved on a generated corpus at the 100k and 1M points using the existing harness, reporting per-step latency and observation size rather than only assembly latency; Reproducibility is proved end to end: the same episode specification and seed produce byte-identical workspace state and an identical verdict across runs and across platforms; Every constituent item retains its capability parent and carries a typed edge to this epic, so the programme is traversable without moving ownership

value.text: Long-horizon agent-environment plan 2026-08-01: pm supplies a framework-neutral substrate, not a training framework. Phase A stabilizes episode identity, deterministic reset, action and observation schemas, verdict predicates, trajectory projection, and point-in-time replay. Phase B adds bounded observation costs, attestation, dataset export, seeded fault and concurrency simulation, and reproducibility across OS and process boundaries. Phase C scales episodes across 100k and 1M-item corpora and thousand-agent fleets with resumable streams, content-addressed shared observations, privacy-safe provenance, and contamination controls. Phase D publishes environment and benchmark authoring kits, offline evaluation adapters, sim-to-real validation hooks, and domain packs. Every phase stays SDK-only, versioned, replayable, and auditable; reward shaping, model policy, and framework-specific orchestration remain external.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Programme note 2026-08-14 — where simulation-to-real transfer sits, and why it is not a fifth seam.

This epic has four seams and takes no more: pm-gd6vnn declares what an agent may observe, pm-e1vkee declares how an outcome is scored, pm-li2fj5 composes those into a reproducible episode, and pm-t8a0x1 is the runnable proof that all three are reachable from published SDK surface alone. Simulation-to-real transfer, which is the remaining workflow named for this programme, is a property of how those four are configured, not a fifth thing to build.

## The property, stated so it can be checked

An environment supports transfer when an episode recorded against a simulated workspace and an episode recorded against a real one are the same object, differing only in which workspace the recipe pointed at. Transfer fails when the simulated episode is cheaper, more deterministic, or more observable than the real one in ways the episode specification does not record, because then a policy trained on the simulation is fitted to the discrepancy.

Three discrepancies are already visible in this project's own record and each is already owned.

The observation ceiling differs. pm-gd6vnn requires an observation to declare both a guaranteed ceiling and a workspace-calibrated expected cost. A three-item simulated workspace and a two-thousand-item real one have the same ceiling and wildly different expected cost, which is exactly the population-adequacy defect pm-s2h0mq measured on the read surfaces. Until expected cost is calibrated per workspace, a simulated episode understates what the real read will cost, and the agent is trained against an observation it will not receive.

The verdict differs by more than the workspace. pm-e1vkee's predicates are computed over recorded state, and a simulated workspace records a state its predicates can always resolve. The finding filed today as pm-xmmafu is the general case: a predicate over a count key that the producer discards when the count is zero resolves on a corpus with defects and stops resolving on a clean one. A simulation is usually the clean one. A reward function that silently stops resolving is worse than one that returns zero.

The step boundary differs. pm-a8lnoh's seeded interleaving harness makes fault injection reproducible, which is the correct substrate for the simulated half. What it does not yet do is state which of the injected faults occur in the real record and at what rate, so a policy can be trained against an interleaving distribution the production system never produces.

## What follows, and what does not

Nothing here is a new item. Each discrepancy is a criterion belonging to a seam that already exists: expected-cost calibration to pm-gd6vnn, resolvability of predicates on a defect-free corpus to pm-e1vkee, and injected-fault rate fidelity to pm-a8lnoh. The right move when any of the four seams is next opened is to add the corresponding criterion there rather than to model transfer as its own deliverable.

The one thing that would be a new seam, and is deliberately not proposed, is a simulator. This programme's claim is that pm is the substrate and the verifier, not that it ships an environment. A simulated workspace is a real workspace with a different recipe, and if that ever stops being true the claim has been lost rather than extended.

value.text: Agent-environment long-range architecture. An episode is a versioned recipe plus content-addressed workspace snapshot, deterministic seed, declared tool and network policy, bounded observation contract, action API, verifier set, reward decomposition, termination rule, and immutable provenance. The SDK must support reset, observe, act, checkpoint, fork, replay, score, and export without requiring the CLI. Trajectories stream observation-action-outcome records with durable cursors and stable episode or agent identities, while secrets and privileged context are redacted before training export. Evaluation separates task success, safety, efficiency, context quality, collaboration, and proof integrity so a scalar reward never hides regressions. The program should support single-agent and multi-agent episodes, offline evaluation, behavior cloning, RL, curriculum generation, adversarial benchmarks, sim-to-real comparisons, counterfactual replay, and human adjudication. Benchmark versions freeze environment, dataset, verifier, and scoring contracts; leakage controls separate training and held-out tasks; uncertainty and inter-rater disagreement remain first-class. Small local fixtures must run in seconds, while fleet orchestration shards episodes, deduplicates snapshots, and aggregates results without changing episode semantics.

value.text: Universal agent-environment contract: define an SDK environment with reset(snapshot/seed), observe(intent/budget), enumerate or validate actions, step(action), reward vector, termination/truncation reason, verifier evidence, and exportable trajectory. A PM item can represent a task, episode, scenario, benchmark case, human decision, or curriculum node without changing core storage semantics; extensions define domain state, action schemas, rewards, simulators, and privacy policies. Record observations, chosen and rejected actions, tool receipts, model/harness/effort when detectable, costs, seeds, environment/build hashes, verifier outputs, and causal PM relationships so offline RL, imitation, preference learning, evals, and failure replay consume the same append-only trajectory format. Separate training, development, and held-out evaluation populations; prevent answer/reward leakage; version tasks and verifiers; support deterministic replay plus explicitly modeled stochastic transitions; report reward components and uncertainty instead of one opaque scalar. Scale curricula with prerequisite graphs, difficulty/novelty sampling, stratified reservoirs, bandit allocation, and regression-triggered cases while preserving tiny ephemeral tasks. Negative controls must show reward hacking, invalid action, stale observation, simulator-to-real divergence, verifier compromise, and benchmark contamination are detected. Sim-to-real promotion requires calibrated transfer evidence, safety constraints, reproducible seeds, and post-deployment measurement, never a narrated equivalence.

value.text: Agent-environment architecture: the public SDK supplies versioned reset, observe, propose-action, apply-action, verify, score, checkpoint, and replay primitives over disposable workspaces. An episode binds a deterministic seed, source revision, schema and policy snapshot, observation budget, allowed action contract, termination predicate, and verifier version into one immutable receipt. Environment adapters may shape rewards, curricula, domain simulators, and partial observability; the pm core provides only recorded state, legal actions, deterministic verdict predicates, provenance, and replay. Fidelity tiers span pure in-memory models, filesystem sandboxes, branch or container replicas, and externally coordinated simulations, but all tiers emit the same streamed observation-action-outcome projection. Evaluation reports success, invariant violations, tokens, latency, retries, nondeterminism, counterfactual regret, and verifier drift separately so a high scalar score cannot hide unsafe behavior.
